subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should these MCP services intentionally share one diagnostic schema, and if so, which owner-neutral module or public seam should own it without coupling the Codex plugin to core internals?
rationale: Source organization and repository policy do not establish whether the differing service prefixes and fields are intentional identities or accidental duplication, so choosing the permanent ownership boundary requires MCP/Codex owner intent.

options.title: Specify contract before refactor
options.body: Keep the adapters separate until examples and golden tests define the shared fields, then extract only the proven common renderer at an approved boundary.

options.title: Approve a shared generic seam
options.body: Explicitly authorize a generic SDK or runtime helper and migrate both owners to it with compatibility and consumer tests.

options.title: Retain service-specific formatting
options.body: Close the cleanup after documenting that each pipeline intentionally owns its diagnostic identity and no shared output contract exists.

recommendation.title: Specify contract before refactor
recommendation.body: Keep the adapters separate until examples and golden tests define the shared fields, then extract only the proven common renderer at an approved boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex context and MCP-adjacent ownership provides the strongest available history signal for deciding the supervision-side contract.
